summary: AE+SE walkthrough of Redwood Optimize focusing on batching strategies, prefix and KV caching, and a cost model tailored to Atlas Financial's heuristics. Customer concerned about latency-sensitive use cases, PSD/regulatory data residency, and predictable unit economics. Discussed hosted vs dedicated trade-offs and proposed pilot with dedicated reserved capacity and KV cache tuning.
topics: Prefix caching vs KV cache for dialog / system prompt reuse
Cost model and token unit economics
Fallbacks, reliability, and dedicated vs hosted
transcript: 00:00 Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for hopping on, i'm jordan from redwood, i'm the AE on this account. quick intro? 00:06 Liam: yeah this is liam, cto at atlas, we want to understand cost/latency tradeoffs for our realtime agent flows. 00:12 Sofia: hi i'm sofia, i run ml infra, mostly interested in kv-cache and batching for our conversation history patterns, 00:20 Priya: great, we'll do a quick 10m product walkthrough then dig into batching and the kv/prefix cache cost model. sound good? 00:28 Raj: yep, thanks. 00:31 Jordan: quick housekeeping - i'll record and share the recording and deck. also we'll send a cost spreadsheet after the call. 00:40 Evan: i'll jump in on the dashboard and cost examples a bit later. 00:44 Liam: perfect. 01:05 Priya: ok starting with assumptions - atlas said you have around 200qps peak, 3k daily active users, average conversation length 6 turns, system prompt ~120 tokens, user prompts average 45 tokens. is that still accurate? 01:18 Sofia: roughly yep, some flows are more latency-sensitive - trading alerts and compliance checks - need <200ms p50 for short prompts. longer summarization can be higher latency. 01:30 Priya: cool. so we typically recommend two levers: batching to improve GPU throughput for non-interactive batched workloads, and prefix/KV caching to avoid recomputing repeated system context. 01:42 Jordan: i'll share an example cost model: raw tokens * model cost per token, but optimized cost = tokens served - cached tokens + batching efficiency factor. 01:50 Priya: example: for a 13B model on A100, naive per-token cost is X, but with prefix cache we can avoid re-sending 120-token system prompt for every request in a session; that saves ~30% of token cost for convo-heavy flows. 02:03 Sofia: is that cache in-memory on the GPU? 02:06 Priya: good question - the KV cache lives in RAM/GPU memory depending on deployment. for hosted we do a hybrid: prefix matching and cached KV on serving nodes; for dedicated/private we can pin cache to instance groups with configurable TTL. 02:20 Raj: how do you handle cache invalidation when user context changes? 02:24 Priya: we have policies - session-level TTL and explicit eviction APIs; you can also set prefix keys by hashing the prompt template and user id. 02:33 Liam: what about cold-starts? 02:36 Priya: cold-starts for new sessions will pay full token cost; we recommend warm-up prefetch for high-value cohorts and background warming during onboarding. 02:45 Jordan: switching to batching - two modes: synchronous small-batch (lower latency, small win) and asynchronous aggregation windows (higher throughput). for your 200qps, dynamic batching with a short 10-30ms window tends to give good throughput without blowing p50. 03:00 Sofia: 10-30ms seems risky for alerting flows. we can't add latency on the critical path. 03:05 Priya: understood; you can route latency-sensitive endpoints to low-latency pools (dedicated or realtime tier) and route bulk/non-critical to batched pools - policy-based routing. 03:15 Raj: can you show the dashboard where we tune batching and see cost impact? 03:20 Evan: sure, opening the Optimize dashboard - here we have model-by-route latency, batching factor, tokens saved from cache, and estimated monthly spend. 03:32 Evan: (screen) you can see this hypothetical route 'alerts' pinned to dedicated low-latency pool; batching factor is 1.1 (minimal) and cost is higher, p50 90ms. route 'summaries' uses batch window 50ms, batching factor 4.2, cost per 1M tokens down 60%. 03:55 Sofia: the 'tokens saved from cache' chart - how is that computed? 03:59 Evan: we instrument prefix matches and KV hits; tokens saved = matched_prefix_length * count_of_matches; we then compute cost saved at the model's per-token rate plus GPU cycles. 04:12 Liam: ok show me a concrete cost calc for our traffic. 04:15 Priya: sure - quick numbers: assume 200qps peak, 6 turns/session, avg user tokens 45, system 120. naive monthly tokens = 200 * 3600 * 24 * 30 * avg_tokens ~ big number. with 30% of system tokens cached and batching saving 35% on generation tokens across batched routes, net spend drops ~40-50% in this model. 04:40 Sofia: that sounds optimistic, what's the sensitivity? small changes in hit-rate will swing savings. 04:45 Priya: exactly - we include sensitivity knobs in the spreadsheet we send; hit-rate, TTL, batch-window, and % of traffic eligible for batching are all variables. 05:00 Jordan: also note quantization recommendations - moving to int8/4 quantized variants can reduce GPU costs but may affect quality; Optimize flags model variants and suggests A/B rollout. 05:12 Sofia: can you do per-route quality guards? we can't degrade accuracy for compliance checks. 05:16 Priya: yes, we support per-route model pinning and quality monitors; we can fire regression alerts tied to eval sets. 05:25 Raj: network/Egress - if we go private, how does KV cache work across VPC? 05:29 Priya: for private deployment the control plane is customer-managed; KV cache can be colocated in the same VPC or on-prem. we support HSM/KMS for encryption at rest and transit; audit logs recorded to your logging destination. 05:43 Nora: from privacy, we need guarantees on retention, and the ability to purge session history. 05:48 Evan: you can set retention at the route level and trigger purge APIs; we also provide audit trails for deletions. 06:00 Liam: i want to see a trade-off: hosted vs dedicated for us. 06:05 Jordan: hosted is fastest to spin up and easy for POC, but dedicated gives you reserved capacity and predictable p50 with lower unit cost at scale. for Atlas, if you're committed to sustained traffic, Dedicated with KV caching pinned to the group looks best. 06:20 Sofia: what's the expected upfront commitment and how quickly can we migrate? 06:24 Jordan: typical dedicated contracts are monthly reserved vGPU hours; migration can be weeks depending on network and compliance checks. pilot usually 2-4 weeks. 06:33 Priya: here's a small benchmark we ran against a sample convo pattern - latency distribution and GPU utilization. note the batched pool achieves 3-4x throughput at acceptable tail latency for non-interactive routes. 06:48 Raj: and autoscaling? 06:51 Priya: we support autoscale policies with warm buffers and burst pools; also automatic fallback to hosted pools if capacity runs out - with policy controls. 07:05 Sofia: how do we ensure determinism for billing? 07:09 Evan: our billing ties to token meters and model variant usage; Optimize provides per-route cost estimates and reconciles with actual usage. 07:19 Liam: curious about the KV cache hit-rate monitoring - how is that surfaced? 07:23 Evan: we show hit-rate trends per route, and you can drill into example requests that missed to tune templates. 07:31 Sofia: any gotchas with conversation length growth increasing cache pressure? 07:35 Priya: yes long running sessions cause KV growth; we recommend sliding-window pruning and compacting histories to embeddings for long-term memory. 07:46 Jordan: wrapping up demos - i'll recap recommended pilot: 1) 2-week dedicated trial for 'alerts' and 'summaries' routes, 2) Priya to run benchmark on sample data, 3) configure KV cache with session TTL 24h and prefix hashing; 4) A/B test quantized variant for 'summaries' only. 08:05 Liam: sounds good. 08:08 Nora: need SOC2 docs and data residency proof before we go to pilot. 08:12 Jordan: we'll send SOC2 and Private deployment artifacts. 08:15 Sofia: also include a clear rollback plan if quality regressions detected. 08:18 Priya: yes automated rollback and traffic split rules are standard. 08:22 Jordan: ok next steps as listed in the follow-up items - we'll email the spreadsheet and calendar invite for pilot kickoff. 08:30 Liam: thanks everyone. 08:32 Jordan: thanks, bye. 46:00 (end)
